proposals.claim: Spread collar shirts should not pair contrast cuffs with unlined collar construction
proposals.rationale: Spread collars with wider angles require balanced visual weight; unlined collars appear flat and delicate while contrast cuffs draw attention downward, creating visual discord and suggesting mismatched garment assembly
constraints: Requires documentation of collar construction methods (lined vs unlined)
Requires visual design guidelines or historical construction standards

proposals.claim: Half-sleeve or rolled-sleeve designs should not feature button-through plackets designed for full-length sleeves
proposals.rationale: Button-through plackets are engineered for continuous arm coverage; half-sleeves expose forearm and create non-functional placket segments, indicating design misalignment or incomplete pattern grading
constraints: Requires sleeve length specifications and measurements

proposals.claim: Shirts designed for untucked wear should measure 2-3 inches shorter than tucked-fit equivalents to maintain proportional silhouettes
proposals.rationale: Untucked shirts require shorter hem lengths to avoid overwhelming proportions; equal length creates excess fabric and visual bulk, indicating design specification mismatch
constraints: Requires documented measurement standards for tucked vs untucked styles
Needs size chart specifications for different wear styles
evidenceNeeded: Size chart documentation by wear style

proposals.claim: Narrow collar styles (under 2.5 inches spread) should not be paired with wide button-through plackets exceeding 1.5 inches width
proposals.rationale: Narrow collars create delicate visual framing; wide plackets dominate the front closure area, causing proportional imbalance and suggesting incomplete design coordination

proposals.claim: French cuffs should only appear on tailored or slim-fit shirts; they are incompatible with oversized or relaxed-fit constructions
proposals.rationale: French cuffs require precise wrist measurement alignment and crisp cuff stands; oversized sleeves prevent proper cuff closure and appearance, indicating misaligned design intent
constraints: Requires fit category definitions and specifications
evidenceNeeded: Sleeve taper specifications by fit type

proposals.claim: Contrast cuffs must coordinate with collar treatment; solid-color unlined collars should not pair with contrast cuffs featuring patterns or different weaves
proposals.rationale: Visual balance requires coordinated design; mismatched treatments between collar and cuff suggest incomplete design review or manufacturing error
constraints: Requires cuff fabric and pattern documentation

proposals.claim: Half-sleeve constructions (finished at mid-forearm) should utilize cuff-band closures only, never button-through plackets
proposals.rationale: Button-through plackets require extended sleeve coverage for functional button placement; half-sleeves cannot accommodate proper button placement, indicating design incompatibility

proposals.claim: Structured, heavily-starched collars should only appear on fitted or tailored shirt bodies, not on relaxed or oversized cuts
proposals.rationale: Structured collars require precise shoulder and neck measurements to sit properly; oversized bodies create collar separation and rolling, indicating foundational design mismatch
constraints: Requires collar starch and stiffness specifications
Requires fit category and body measurement standards
